newsitem.title: BULGARIA: FORECAST -Bulgaria 1996 inflation seen at 240 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST -Bulgaria 1996 inflation seen at 240 pct.

text.p: Bulgaria's annual inflation for this year is likely to rise to 240 precent, more than doubling the government's previous assumption of 104 percent, the National Statistics Institute said on Thursday.
"Our preliminary estimates show that monthly inflation until the end of the year will be around 10 percent," NSI director Zahari Karamfilov told a news confernce.
With cumulative inflation for the first nine months at 153 percent, inflation by year-end will reach 240 percent, if the monthly rate is 10 percent, said the NSI.
Bulgaria's monthly consumer price inflation quickened to 18.8 percent in September from 17.1 percent in August.
Inflation in the automn months usually picks up due to increased spending on fuel imports and heating and it would be difficult to curb inflation then, economists say.

Bulgaria topped twice its budget frame targets for this year. Under a revised budget frame in June the annual central interest rate was seen at 67 percent, a long way down from the current 240 percent.

The central bank hiked the main interest rate to an all-time high of 300 percent in September in a bid to stabilize the crumbling financial system. The rate was cut last week by 60 percent to ease the burden to on domestic debt payments.
